idiom_name: stand-in object + creation hook + single-flight guard
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: the stand-in implements the same interface as the real object, holds only what construction needs (identifier, path, parameters, factory), and forwards each request through a guard that builds the real subject on the first call and caches it. Keep the construction itself in a separate hook (factory, supplier, lambda) so that retry policy, instrumentation and failure semantics stay in one place, and make the guard single-flight instead of hand-rolling double-checked locking. The classic structure is still justified when the stand-in must implement several operations or when clients observe identity; where the runtime already offers a lazy value (Lazy<T>, by lazy, lazy val, cached_property, sync.OnceValue, OnceLock) prefer that primitive plus a forwarding member.
code_sketch:
proxy = StandIn(id)              # cheap: holds only the construction input
proxy.operation(args)            # guard builds the real subject once, then forwards
#   guard: real = cache.get() or build_once(factory, id)
#   never: real = new Expensive(id) at each call site
pitfalls: Triggering construction on every access instead of caching it - or caching it somewhere the guard does not check - rebuilds the expensive object repeatedly.
Hand-rolled check-then-act guards race: two threads both see the uninitialized state and both build; use the runtime's once/lazy primitive or a proper lock around the build.
Forwarding the work but not the identity: without equals/hashCode/toString and type forwarding the stand-in breaks sets, maps, assertions, serialization and ORM identity.

Wrong move: treat the stand-in as inert until a business call arrives -> failure: lifecycle and identity touches (equals/hashCode, toString, logging, a getter after the session closes) trigger or fail initialization - Hibernate throws LazyInitializationException outside the session, sometimes from a log statement alone -> instead define which operations may act on the unmaterialized stand-in (identifier access, identity) and initialize deliberately inside the owning context.

Wrong move: paper over late initialization by letting the stand-in open its own session (Open Session in View, hibernate.enable_lazy_load_no_trans) -> failure: innocent object graphs walk off into N+1 query storms with no visible call site -> instead fetch what the use case needs up front (JOIN FETCH, entity graphs) or project to DTOs, keeping lazy access a deliberate, measured path.

Wrong move: construct the stand-in at each call site or render pass -> failure: every use gets a fresh proxy with its own guard, so the real object is rebuilt repeatedly and caches/identity break (React re-creates the lazy type and remounts the subtree when lazy() is declared inside a component) -> instead declare the stand-in once in a stable scope (module top level, container registration) so all uses share one cached real subject.
